Preparing a transactional repair plan for %1$s. The database is not modified during analysis.
Issues to repair: %1$s. MDBX2 creates a recovery snapshot first, then writes and rechecks everything in one transaction.
Choose how to resolve the conflict
Keep current content and remove invalid deletion markers
Delete the conflicting item (identity verification required)
Canceling stops the entire repair without writing any changes to the database.
Serious issues require manual review or recovery from another source. Monica has not modified the affected content.
The content still exists, but the database also has a deletion marker. Keeping the content removes the invalid marker; deleting it removes the content and creates a valid deletion record.
The object was deleted without a sync deletion marker. This can usually be repaired automatically.
The same object has multiple deletion markers. They can usually be consolidated automatically.
Chunk issues: %1$s. Use diagnostics to check the affected content
The database has no attachments, so no chunk checks are needed
Attachments with matching chunk indexes and content: %1$s
MDBX 2 uses incremental sync; the remote .mdbx is only an encrypted bootstrap copy
MDBX 2 uses the Rust engine and local encrypted storage
MDBX 1 retains the existing compatible format and whole-file sync
Monica cannot currently open the database file. It may have moved, access permissions may have changed, or a remote copy may still be downloading.
Database content is unavailable, and further sync attempts may fail.
Check that the file is still in its original location and allow Monica to access the folder
Finish downloading or syncing remote databases before checking again
If it remains unreadable, keep the current file and open the latest healthy backup
The internal structure failed basic checks, possibly because of an interrupted write, file damage, or an incomplete copy.
Further writes may affect more content, and some existing content may be unreadable.
Copy the file or export a full backup first to preserve its current state
Close other devices or cloned app instances using this database, then check again
If the problem persists, restore a healthy snapshot or migrate readable content to a new database
The database is open, but header authentication requires it to remain unlocked with keys available.
This usually does not indicate data damage; the full check has not finished yet.
Unlock Monica and keep the database open
Tap Check again to complete authentication
If repeated unlocks do not help, open diagnostics and maintenance for details
The database header authentication information does not match its content.
The file may be an incomplete copy, use the wrong key, or be damaged. Further writes carry a high risk to data.
Keep a copy of the current file and pause writes from other devices
Verify the credentials used to open the database and the source of the file
Prefer restoring a verified snapshot or backup
The index used for fast integrity checks is being created for the first time or needs an unlocked database to continue.
The database is usually still usable, but health check results are incomplete.
Keep the database unlocked and wait for the current operation to finish
Avoid opening the same file in multiple cloned app instances at once
The integrity index is out of sync with the current database content.
Fast check results are temporarily unreliable. Interrupted writes or concurrent access may be involved.
Create a full snapshot or export a backup first
Close the same database in other app instances or devices, then reopen and unlock it
If a new check still reports issues, restore a healthy snapshot
A commit or branch points to a history node missing from the current file.
Commit history, comparisons, or restoring older versions may have gaps.
Complete a sync on every device that uses this database
Open commit history and identify the latest available commit
If checking again does not resolve it, restore a healthy snapshot from before the gap
Commit records need available keys to verify their authenticity.
Only the verification prerequisites are missing; no content mismatch has been found yet.
Keep the database open and check again
Avoid restoring from this commit until verification finishes
A commit authentication tag does not match the recorded content.
The history node may be damaged. Comparing or restoring from it may produce incorrect results.
Create a full backup of the current database first
Locate healthy nodes before and after the issue in commit history
Restore a healthy snapshot or migrate currently accessible entries to a new database
Recorded attachment chunk counts or order do not match the stored content.
Affected attachments may not open, export, or sync completely.
Export important attachments that can still be opened
Finish a remote sync, then check attachments again
If problems persist, restore a backup containing complete attachments
A snapshot failed checks of its digest, authentication information, or content structure.
This snapshot is unsuitable for recovery; the current database may still be unaffected.
Do not restore from the affected snapshot
Create a new full snapshot and verify its status
When recovery is needed, choose another verified snapshot
Content is missing its parent folder
Some entries or attachments reference folders missing from the current database.
Affected content may be absent from normal lists, and moving or syncing it may fail.
Finish syncing all devices and check again
Copy accessible content to a valid folder or a new database
Restore the latest healthy snapshot if the content cannot be accessed
Category rules do not match content
A category has no valid configuration or contains content types its rules do not allow.
Affected content may appear on the wrong page or fail to edit and sync as expected.
Finish syncing, then check the category again
Move affected content to the correct category or a regular folder
If the category is invalid, back up its content before recreating it
The same object has multiple deletion markers, so its current deletion state is ambiguous.
Affected content may conflict during sync, recovery, or permanent deletion.
Create a full snapshot or export a complete backup first
Finish a sync on every device using this database, then check again
If the issue persists, restore a healthy snapshot or migrate usable content to a new database
Content is marked as deleted but has no matching deletion history record.
Other devices may not recognize the deletion correctly. Content may reappear or cause conflicts.
Finish syncing every device and check again
If the issue remains, restore a healthy snapshot from before the deletion
Content that is still in use also has deletion markers, creating a conflicting state.
Later syncs may treat valid content as deleted again.
Immediately back up affected content that is still accessible
Pause editing on other devices and complete a sync
If the issue persists, restore a healthy snapshot or copy content to a new database
A device acknowledgment of a deletion record failed history relationship checks.
Sync may repeatedly process deletions or retain records pending cleanup for too long.
Make sure the affected devices finish syncing and close the database
Sync again on this device and check for conflicts
If the issue persists, retain the logs and restore a healthy backup
Permanent deletion records do not match database objects or deletion markers.
Devices may be unable to agree on permanent deletion state.
Finish syncing all devices and check again
Keep copies of the current database and logs
If the issue persists, restore a healthy backup from before the permanent deletion
A device records a latest commit position that is missing, outdated, or belongs to another device.
Cross-device sync may miss updates, and commit history may show an incorrect position.
Let every device still in use finish syncing one at a time
Confirm the latest valid node in commit history
If a new check still reports issues, reestablish sync from a common healthy snapshot
A device has been inactive for a long time
The database retains a device record that has not participated in sync for some time.
This is a status notice and usually does not affect database content.
Check whether the device still uses this database
If it is still in use, let it finish a sync
If it is retired, you can keep using the database with the record retained and clean it up during later maintenance
This version has no specific explanation for this engine diagnostic yet.
The impact depends on the check category shown in technical details.
Close other devices or cloned app instances, then check again
If the issue persists, export Monica logs and keep the technical details for investigation
